data.body:
Detail moved out of the description to fit the 8,000-char admission cap (no figure or decision changed):

called with the boto3 `bedrock-runtime` client's `invoke_model` and a JSON body of `{"inputText": ..., "dimensions": 1024, "normalize": true}` (input limit 8,192 tokens / 50,000 characters, so the summary is truncated to 40,000 characters before the call), region from `rebar.toml` `[llm] bedrock_region_name` (currently `us-east-1`, rebar.toml:213), boto3 reaching the venv through the `bedrock` extra's `pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]`. Cosine similarity by brute force; 630 normalized vectors need no ANN library.

read from commit **f147e08242f** (parent of 2de5f341ec4, which deleted them). The prompt TEXT is `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/ticket_digest.md` at that SHA; the contract is in `src/rebar/llm/contracts.py`. Both are absent from current main, hence the pinned commit.

Model: the **`trivial`** class (`src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py`, default `claude-haiku-4-5`, overridable by `REBAR_LLM_TRIVIAL_MODEL`), resolved id recorded in the fixture header.

`infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf` (sid `ConverseAnthropicClaudeOnly`) scopes `bedrock:InvokeModel` to `anthropic.claude-*` foundation-model and inference-profile ARNs only; no Titan or embedding ARN is granted anywhere in `infra/`. So `amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0` returns `AccessDeniedException` there — the shape ADR 0059:307 records for an unentitled id. Candidate 2's `claude-haiku-4-5` is entitled; candidate 3 is not.

Build the fixture at a pinned tickets-branch SHA so the set is reproducible: collect every recorded `duplicates` link (`rebar list --full --exclude-deleted -o json`, reading each ticket's `deps`; relation vocabulary in `docs/ticket-model.md`), close transitively into clusters, enumerate within-cluster pairs, and 

 **Only the prompt text and the output shape are reused — the deleted `overlap/` orchestration is NOT restored**; the eval calls the model directly through the existing `rebar.llm` runner, and no file under `src/rebar/llm/overlap/` is reinstated.

One call per ticket, **fed exactly the fixture's `digest_input` field** (the full title + description + every comment the original prompt consumed, per epic 62dc's architecture comment — NOT a truncated description), and the returned `TicketDigest` JSON is **committed to `evals/similar-tickets/digests.json`**, keyed by ticket id plus a SHA-256 of `digest_input` and the prompt text. The runner reuses a cached digest whenever that key matches and only calls the model on a miss, so the recorded recall tables are recomputable from the committed fixture with no model access.
